source: Expanding Edge grant eligibility quiz (adapted for OSMF Research Tracker)

items.name: Environmental Farm Plan (EFP)
items.desc: A free, confidential risk assessment of your land and practices. Nearly every cost-share program below either requires a current EFP or scores applications higher when one is on file — usually the first move regardless of which project you pick.
items.note: Delivered by AFSC (Alberta), the Investment Agriculture Foundation (BC), or the Ministry of Agriculture (Saskatchewan) depending on province.

items.name: SCAP On-Farm Stewardship (AFSC)
items.desc: Alberta's delivery of the federal-provincial Sustainable CAP framework, covering water quality protection, biodiversity, and manure management improvements for registered producers.
items.note: Delivered through AFSC. Requires a current EFP. Confirm the active stream and intake window before designing a project around it.

items.name: Beaver Hills Biosphere Rural Residential Stewardship
items.desc: One of the few programs open to acreage and hobby-farm owners, not just commercial producers. Covers wetland enhancement, riparian planting, and native species establishment — a strong fit for Sturgeon Watershed clients specifically.
items.note: Regional program tied to the Beaver Hills Biosphere area east of Edmonton. Confirm your property falls inside the boundary.

items.name: Watershed Resiliency and Restoration Program (WRRP)
items.desc: Funded wetland, riparian, and floodplain restoration at the watershed scale. Applications go through municipalities, First Nations, or non-profit watershed groups, not directly to individual landowners.
items.note: Not renewed in the 2026-27 Alberta budget and currently closed to new applications. Where it reopens, individual clients would still need to route a project through a partner organization such as a watershed stewardship group.

items.name: Ducks Unlimited Canada — landowner programs
items.desc: Wetland restoration, forage establishment, and conservation easement programs for landowners willing to protect or restore wetland habitat. Often layers alongside a provincial stewardship program.
items.note: Coverage and payment structure vary significantly by region — confirm local program presence before quoting a client.

items.name: Alberta Conservation Association — Landowner Habitat Program
items.desc: Pays landowners to retain habitat on their property for a 5–20 year term, in exchange for reasonable public foot access. Less a construction cost-share and more a habitat-retention income stream that can offset design and stewardship work.
items.note: Best positioned as a complementary revenue stream alongside a restoration or design project, not a standalone funding source for construction.

items.name: BC Beneficial Management Practices (BMP) Program
items.desc: BC's flagship cost-share for water infrastructure, riparian works, and construction projects tied to an Environmental Farm Plan. Covers irrigation, riparian buffers, and water projects at a high cost-share rate.
items.note: Currently closed to new applications except the Extreme Weather Preparedness category. Worth tracking for the next intake window.

items.name: Saskatchewan Farm Stewardship Program (FSP)
items.desc: Cost-shares beneficial management practices including shelterbelt and windbreak planting, riparian fencing and buffers, and wetland restoration.
items.note: Most categories require a current Environmental Farm Plan. Cost-share rates and caps are set per practice category.

items.name: Farm and Ranch Water Infrastructure Program (FRWIP)
items.desc: Rebates for dugouts, pipelines, wells, and small dams under 2.5 metres, covering the kind of on-farm water storage and delivery infrastructure that pairs naturally with a pond or swale build.
items.note: Structured as a post-construction rebate, not pre-approved grant funding — the client pays first and claims the rebate against invoices.

items.name: ALUS Canada community programs
items.desc: Pays farmers and ranchers per acre to convert marginal or environmentally sensitive land into wetlands, buffers, and grassland. Delivered through local chapters rather than a single national application.
items.note: Chapter coverage varies by region — confirm whether an active ALUS chapter operates near the client's property before including it in a proposal.

items.name: Resilient Agricultural Landscape Program (RALP)
items.cap: $150,000 producers · $300,000 grazing associations / community pastures / approved Indigenous applicants
items.desc: Alberta's largest direct landscape-stewardship grant for producers — covers rotational grazing infrastructure, riparian work, perennial forage, shelterbelts, eco-buffers, pollinator habitat, and wetlands. Requires a current EFP and at least $25,000 in annual farm commodities.
items.note: Currently closed. When it reopens, note that funding is calculated per BMP, not a flat percentage of any project the client proposes — and accredited technical support has its own eligibility rules.

items.name: Alberta Water Program — On-Farm Water Supply
items.desc: Covers wells, dugouts, spring development, dams, cisterns, unshared pipelines, crop-irrigation water sources, and off-site livestock watering. Also carries special incentives for well decommissioning, well-pit conversion, and wetland assessments.
items.note: Requires responsibility for input costs on an Alberta operation with at least $25,000 in annual farm commodities.

items.name: Alberta Water Program — On-Farm Irrigation
items.desc: Cost-shares new irrigation-system purchases and upgrades for producers who own an irrigated agricultural operation.
items.note: Excludes projects already funded for the same type on the same parcel.

items.name: On-Farm Efficiency Program (OFEP)
items.cap: $150,000 total per applicant (2024–28) · sub-caps by category
items.desc: Smart farm technology, energy efficiency, farm security, and efficient grain handling. Sub-caps: Smart Farm Technology $50,000, Energy Efficiency $50,000, Farm Security $2,000, Efficient Grain Handling $100,000.
items.note: Closed until 2026. Worth flagging to clients planning solar or efficiency upgrades for the next intake.

items.name: Growing Greenhouses Program
items.desc: Supports new construction or expansion of commercial greenhouses and vertical farms, including energy-efficient construction, advanced lighting, automation, and renewable-energy technology.
items.note: New builds need a minimum $2 million total project investment; existing facilities must increase annual food production by at least 10%. Currently closed.

items.name: Agricultural Clean Technology — Adoption Stream (ACT)
items.costShare: Up to 40% (50/50 for majority under-represented ownership)
items.desc: Cost-shares commercially available clean technology with measurable environmental benefits — GHG, fertilizer, or methane reductions. Applicant must already have its own cost-share secured.
items.note: Adoption Stream intake is currently closed; the prior intake required project completion by March 31, 2026.

items.name: Agricultural Clean Technology — Research & Innovation Stream
items.costShare: Up to 50% (60% for majority under-represented ownership)
items.desc: Funds research and innovation rather than routine implementation. This is more relevant to Expanding Edge as the applicant developing a new method or technology than as a client-facing grant — worth tracking separately from the farmer-facing results.
items.note: Current intake is closed; an Accelerator pathway through initial recipient organizations remains open.

items.name: Alberta Innovates — Agriculture & Environment Program
items.desc: Continuous-intake applied research and technology-development funding covering Sustainable AgTech, Climate Smart Agriculture, Water Innovation, and Land Management Solutions. Open to technology developers, SMEs, researchers, and individuals, not just registered producers.
items.note: Better suited to a research/technology angle (e.g. a water-modeling or land-assessment tool) than a routine design-and-build project.

items.name: Rangeland Sustainability Program (RSP)
items.desc: Supports collaborative rangeland conservation, research, education, and beneficial-management-practice development. Individuals cannot apply directly but can collaborate with an eligible academic, Indigenous, municipal, or non-profit applicant.
items.note: Best positioned as a partnership opportunity — pair the client with a ranching association, municipality, or university before applying.

items.name: Ecosystem Services Grant Program
items.costShare: Grant to delivery organization — no standard landowner rate
items.desc: Funds organizations delivering ecosystem-services programs on high-value natural assets at risk of conversion, without requiring a perpetual conservation agreement. The organization enrolls and works with landowners directly.
items.note: A pilot program; current intake is closed with the next round expected spring 2026. Landowners don't apply directly — route through the delivering organization.

items.name: Private Land Conservation Program
items.costShare: Grant to land trust — no standard landowner rate
items.desc: Funds Alberta-based land trusts to establish and steward term conservation easements on native landscapes, habitat corridors, riparian systems, wetlands, and watershed functions. The 2026 application requires forest, shrub, grassland, riparian/wetland, pasture, and development-area mapping.
items.note: The landowner works with a land trust rather than applying directly; perpetual easements and land purchases are not eligible, only term easements and stewardship. Next intake expected spring 2026.

items.name: Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP)
items.costShare: Financing, not a grant — repaid through property tax
items.desc: Lets property owners finance solar and energy-efficiency upgrades, repaid over time through the property-tax system, rather than a direct cost-share.
items.note: Only available where the client's municipality participates — confirm local enrollment before proposing this as a funding source.

items.name: Alberta Micro-Generation
items.costShare: Not a grant — net billing/credit framework
items.desc: A regulatory framework letting Alberta electricity customers generate their own power (solar, wind, etc.) and receive billing credit, rather than a cost-share program.
items.note: Useful to mention alongside CEIP so a client doesn't overestimate available 'government funding' for solar.

items.name: Supply Management Processing Investment Fund (SMPIF)
items.desc: For dairy, poultry, egg, and hatchery processors investing in productivity and efficiency, including equipment to reduce water and energy consumption and equipment to treat wastewater from increased production. A strong fit for Expanding Edge's water/wastewater design work if the client is a processor, not a farm.
items.note: Not a general sustainability-planning grant — the project must be a processing investment, and application prep and feasibility studies are explicitly ineligible. Construction costs are generally ineligible for non-dairy applicants. Open through March 31, 2028.

items.name: Indigenous Forestry Initiative
items.desc: Funds Indigenous communities and organizations for sustainable forest-management planning, forest-policy development, and free-prior-and-informed-consent activities. A potential forest-stewardship-planning and GIS/landscape-assessment service line for Expanding Edge working with an Indigenous partner.
items.note: Open through September 1, 2028. A broader contribution stream for Indigenous forestry activities is also available alongside this grant.

items.name: FRIAA FireSmart Program
items.desc: The Forest Resource Improvement Association of Alberta runs FireSmart, Community Reforestation, Mountain Pine Beetle, Wildfire Reclamation, and Caribou Habitat Recovery funding. Relevant to Expanding Edge if it builds a fuel-management, vegetation-management, or wildfire-resilient landscape design service.
items.note: A 2026 call for vegetation-management proposals is open with submissions due September 4, 2026. Eligibility depends heavily on applicant type and geography — not a simple rebate for an individual acreage owner.

items.name: AgriMarketing — Market Diversification for SMEs
items.desc: Supports agricultural and agri-food SMEs diversifying into new or non-traditional markets in response to trade barriers. Federally flagged sectors include canola, beef, pork, pulses, horticulture, and fish/seafood. This is a market-development grant, not a farm-infrastructure cost-share — pair it with a water, grazing, or processing program for the physical project.
items.note: Launched February 2026. Requires incorporation/legal-entity documentation and two years of financial statements.

items.name: 2 Billion Trees Program
items.desc: Previously funded tree planting for carbon sequestration, biodiversity, habitat, and flood/wildfire resilience, including projects with for-profit and Indigenous organizations in Alberta.
items.note: The federal government is winding this program down and no longer accepts new applications; existing agreements continue. Keep on file for a successor tree-planting or nature-based climate program.
